newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-MARIUCCI NAMED 49ERS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-MARIUCCI NAMED 49ERS HEAD COACH.

text.p: The San Francisco 49ers named University of California coach Steve Mariucci their head coach Thursday to replace George Seifert who quit Wednesday.
Carmen Policy, 49ers' president, announced Mariucci's appointment at a news conference at team headquarters in Santa Clara, and would not reveal the financial terms of his five-year contract.

"I can't tell you how proud I am," said Mariucci, 41. "I understand what I am getting into. This has been the most successful franchise in pro football over the last 15 years and I understand that I have huge shoes to fill."
Mariucci's only head coaching experience was this past season as head man at the University of California. The team was 6-6 and lost in the Aloha Bowl to Navy.
Before that, Mariucci spent four seasons as an assistant coach with the Green Bay Packers, working strictly with quarterbacks.
Mariucci took the job a day after the 57-year-old Seifert, who guided the 49ers to two Super Bowl wins in eight seasons as head coach, announced his resignation.
The 49ers were 12-4 this season, but lost twice to the Carolina Panthers, a second-year expansion team that unseated them for the NFC West title.
Policy said it was the first time under Eddie DeBartolo's ownership the San Francisco 49ers had signed a head coach for more than three years.

He said the 49ers insisted on offering Mariucci a five-year contract to show their confidence in him "and to allow him to understand that we are going to be patient relative to his development of his programme in his style and with his imprint."

Mariucci said that, before Seifert's resignation, Policy had discussed with him the possibility of Mariucci joining the 49ers as an offensive coordinator with the chance of "becoming the head coach some day when coach Seifert was through."
But that plan suddenly changed Tuesday night when Seifert told Policy he was resigning and Policy offered Mariucci the head coaching job.
"It was the most unusual turn of events here in the last couple of days...We negotiated a contract today. It's happened that fast," Mariucci said.
Policy said the ideal situation would have been for Mariucci to have joined the 49ers as offensive coordinator for a year or two before stepping into the head coach's position.
"It seemed like a plan that was made in heaven," he said.
But when Seifert quit, Policy said he discussed the situation with DeBartolo and they decided "if this young man has upside talents, let's give him a chance now."
